title: Planetary Nebula HDW 3
caption: The planetary nebula HDW 3, imaged by the Mayall 4-meter Telescope
credit: T.A. Rector (University of Alaska Anchorage) and H. Schweiker (WIYN and NOIRLab/NSF/AURA)

recognition.text: Published in the NSF NOIRLab image archive. No published rating.

story: Hartl-Dengel-Weinberger 3, or HDW 3, is a large and ancient planetary nebula in the constellation Perseus, with a distinctive braided shape. The star that produced it is the faint bluish one just below and right of the bright star near the image center.

A planetary nebula is the gas cast off by a dying star of modest mass. HDW 3's braids are thought to come from motion. As the nebula travels through the galaxy, it collides with the interstellar gas around it, and that collision twists and shapes the glowing material.

Older planetary nebulae like this one have expanded and thinned out, which makes them more easily reshaped by their surroundings. The bright star near the center is not the source of the nebula. The true parent is its fainter neighbor.

understand.summary: The Mayall 4-meter Telescope's Mosaic camera used two narrowband filters. Hydrogen-alpha is shown in red and oxygen [O III] in blue.
